example_summary: Mr. Abhishek, a senior citizen, enters a reverse mortgage scheme where his house is mortgaged for monthly payouts, with tax liability deferred until the bank eventually sells the property.
source_provision:
| Transaction Stage | Statutory Section | Statutory Condition | Tax Treatment / Legal Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mortgaging Property | **Section 47(xvi)** | Asset mortgaged under a Central Government notified Reverse Mortgage Scheme | **Not a transfer**; No Capital Gains tax liability |
| Receipt of Loan | **Section 10(43)** | Amount received as loan (lump sum or periodic installments) | **100% Exempt** from Income Tax |
| Property Alienation | **Section 45** | Bank alienates/sells mortgaged property to recover loan on default/maturity | **Taxable Event**; Capital Gains tax triggered at alienation |


- **Exemption from Definition of Transfer [Section 47(xvi)]**: Transfer of a capital asset in a transaction of reverse mortgage notified by the Central Government shall NOT be regarded as a transfer.
- **Exemption of Disbursement [Section 10(43)]**: Any loan amount received by a senior citizen (lump sum or installment) under a reverse mortgage scheme is fully exempt from income tax.
- **Deferral Benchmark**: Tax is not permanently waived on the capital asset, but deferred until actual alienation by the bank for recovery.


> [!IMPORTANT] Recovery Alienation Benchmark: Capital gains tax is not attracted at the time of pledging/mortgaging or receiving installments. It is attracted ONLY at the stage when the bank alienates the mortgaged property to recover the outstanding loan.

director.justification: Reverse mortgage transactions involve statutory exclusions from transfer and taxable income at the mortgaging and receipt stages, overriding standard capital gains until final alienation by the bank.
director.visual_metaphor: A three-stage tax shelter vault shielding mortgaging and monthly payouts, opening only when the bank alienates the house.

beat_plan.beat_goal: Establish Mr. Abhishek mortgaging his residential house to the bank under a notified reverse mortgage scheme for monthly installments.
Examine Section 47(xvi) which explicitly provides that reverse mortgage transfer is not regarded as a transfer for capital gains.
Detail Section 10(43) which renders all loan disbursements, whether monthly or lump sum, completely tax-exempt.
Track the loan maturity default and final stage where bank alienates the property, triggering capital gains under Section 45.
Summarize that mortgaging and payouts attract zero tax, while alienation by bank triggers deferred capital gains.

beats.voice_sync_text: ഇവിടെയാണ് Section 47(xvi) വരുന്നത്. ഈ provision പ്രകാരം, ഒരു notified reverse mortgage scheme-ൽ capital asset transfer ചെയ്യുന്നത് tax purpose-ന് Not Regarded as Transfer ആണ്. അതുകൊണ്ട് തന്നെ ഈ stage-ൽ No Capital Gain tax liability ഉണ്ടാകുന്നില്ല.
